subsystems.name: Conducting circuit
subsystems.role: the moving conductor that cuts the planet's magnetic field and carries the generated current.
parts: cryogenic cooling loop for superconducting variants

subsystems.name: Current-closure path
subsystems.role: completes the circuit so current can actually flow, either through ambient plasma or back along a second conductor.
parts: field-aligned current path through the ionosphere and magnetosphere

subsystems.name: Momentum and orbit management
subsystems.role: the reaction torque pushes the conductor against the planet's rotation, so its orbit and attitude must be actively maintained.

subsystems.name: Power conversion and delivery
subsystems.role: converts the generated current into usable electricity and moves it to a load.
parts: transmission to a surface grid or a beamed-power link

subsystems.name: Environment monitoring
subsystems.role: tracks what extraction is doing to the field, the ionosphere and the planet's rotation rate.
parts: radio ranging to measure spin rate

subsystems.name: Command and control
subsystems.role: coordinates a distributed array and rides out plasma faults and radiation.

buildSteps.title: Characterise the target planet
buildSteps.detail: Map the magnetic field strength and geometry, the plasma density and the radiation belts, and work out where the return current can close.

buildSteps.title: Design the conductor
buildSteps.detail: Choose aluminium or high-temperature superconducting tape, size it for the current and the I²R or cryogenic losses, and harden it against radiation and atomic oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Deploy it in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Launch the conductor spooled, then unreel it using gravity-gradient and centrifugal forces until it hangs radially, tens to thousands of kilometres long.

buildSteps.title: Complete the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Fire plasma contactors at each end, or connect the return conductor, so a closed current path exists between the conductor and the planet's plasma environment.

buildSteps.title: Extract power
buildSteps.detail: Because the magnetic field co-rotates with the planet while the conductor is held fixed in inertial space, the relative motion drives an electromotive force; current flows and power is drawn from the circuit.

buildSteps.title: Deal with the reaction torque
buildSteps.detail: The I×B force opposes the relative motion, so the conductor absorbs angular momentum from the planet. It must be re-boosted with thrusters or allowed to change orbit — either way the momentum has to go somewhere.

buildSteps.title: Scale to an array
buildSteps.detail: Stack many conductors, or build a continuous equatorial ring, to raise output; a planet with a strong field and fast rotation needs far less hardware per megawatt.

buildSteps.title: Deliver the power
buildSteps.detail: Condition the electricity and send it to a surface grid by cable or beamed link, or use it in orbit for propulsion and industry.

buildSteps.title: Manage planetary side effects
buildSteps.detail: Track day length, core–mantle coupling and field strength over decades, since draining rotational energy ultimately slows the planet and may load the dynamo that makes the field.

prerequisites.why: tethers have generated current in low Earth orbit, but long deployments have also failed, and nothing has run at planetary scale.
a tether only produces power if the circuit closes through the surrounding plasma or a return conductor.
low-loss conductors make the circuit efficient, and they must survive radiation and thermal cycling in space.

prerequisites.tech: Large space structures and orbital assembly
prerequisites.why: a multi-kilometre conductor or a ring has to be deployed and kept stable under changing forces.
without it, the long-term cost of despinning a planet — day length and magnetic field — cannot be predicted.

pathway.milestone: planetary magnetosphere missions and tether physics research, with Io's flux tube as the natural worked example
pathway.unlocks: Io drives millions of amperes through Jupiter's field every second, showing that a body moving through a co-rotating magnetosphere really does couple mechanically to the planet's spin.

pathway.milestone: a purpose-built power-generating tether demonstration, first in low Earth orbit then in a strong planetary field
pathway.unlocks: measured watts out, plus real numbers for tether losses, plasma closure and momentum management.

pathway.milestone: megawatt-class tether array in a giant planet's magnetosphere
pathway.unlocks: a fast-rotating planet with an enormous field needs the least conductor per unit of power, making it the first credible site.

pathway.milestone: equatorial ring arrays delivering terawatts, and only then deliberate planetary spin control
pathway.unlocks: civilisation-scale power, at the cost of a lengthening day and an uncertain effect on the planet's magnetic field.
